chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribaat, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one upon whom is a debt, so he intends to fulfil it, he would have two Protectors from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, assisting him upon the payment of his entrustment. So if his intention is deficient regarding the payment, they are deficient in assisting him by the measure of what he reduces from his intention.'
ai.seo_question: How does intention affect divine assistance in paying off debt?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual mechanics of debt repayment, linking material ease to the sincerity of one's intention (niyyah). This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between divine aid and human agency, where the 'two protectors' symbolize the spiritual support granted to those committed to fulfilling their financial trusts (amanat).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Rabaat who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one upon whom was a debt, so he intends to fulfil it, he would have two Protectors from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic assisting him upon the payment of his entrustment. So if he is deficient in his intention about the payment, so the assistance is reduced from him by a measurement of what he reduces from his intention’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Ribat who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

If one is indebted and he intends to pay it back, from the side of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, there will be two guards to help him to keep his trust; but if his intention falls short they also fall behind in their help proportionate to the degree of the fall of his intention.”’
